headline: KINROSS Q3 TONIGHT: $0.49 EPS AND $2.1B REVENUE ON THE LINE AS GOLD MINERS FALL ON GOOD NUMBERS
snippet: Kinross Gold reports Q3 2026 results after market close today, with the Street expecting $0.49 EPS and $2.08 billion in revenue from approximately 425,000 gold-equivalent ounces produced. Cost pressure is the key risk — attributable AISC rose 24% year-on-year to $1,336/oz in Q2 — and Newmont's recent Q3 beat followed by a stock selloff shows the sector may be pricing in disappointment regardless of the numbers. Teck Resources follows tomorrow (Oct. 29) at pre-market.

headline: BOSS ENERGY HONEYMOON: 61% URANIUM JUMP TO 1.41M LB IN FY2026; SAFETY SLIPS, CEO SAYS 'IMPROVEMENT REQUIRED'
snippet: Boss Energy's FY2026 sustainability report (Oct. 28) confirms 1.41 million pounds of uranium oxide produced at Honeymoon — up 61% year-on-year and the company's first full year of output — while revenue more than doubled to $151.1 million with no debt. The safety picture worsened: the total recordable injury frequency rate rose to 19.66 from 12.8 and the CEO openly acknowledges performance requires improvement. FY2027 guidance of 1.25–1.3 million lbs at $83–92/lb AISC signals a near-term output dip as operations are optimized.

headline: WHY GOLD MINERS KEEP FALLING EVEN AFTER RECORD PROFITS — Radomski: Sector Decline Has Further to Go
snippet: Kitco's Radomski dissects the disconnect between gold miner earnings — Newmont posted record Q3 adjusted net income — and share prices that keep falling anyway. With major mining ETFs down 9–10% in recent weeks while gold itself held near $4,000, the piece argues the sector is still under distribution pressure and warns retail investors that strong earnings alone are not enough to stop the selling.

headline: HAYWOOD CUTS GOLD FORECAST TO $4,345 BUT CALLS MINERS 'ATTRACTIVE' AT 7.83X CASH FLOW
snippet: Haywood Securities trimmed its 2026 average gold price forecast from $4,906 to $4,345 per ounce following Q2 weakness but maintained a constructive view on gold equities, which now trade at 7.83x forward cash flow — below their five-year average of 8.86x. The firm calls it a structural bull market in consolidation and names Equinox Gold as its top senior producer pick, with First Mining Gold and Thesis Gold & Silver as developer picks.

headline: AVINO DRILLS 616 g/t Ag OVER 4.86m AT LA PRECIOSA — 23.6m Mineralized Zone at Vein Junction, Mexico (TSX:ASM)
snippet: Avino Silver & Gold (TSX:ASM) reported high-grade silver from its La Preciosa drilling in Mexico, with the highlight interval returning 616 g/t silver over 4.86 metres at a vein junction within a broader 23.60-metre mineralized zone. The result (Oct. 26) adds to the ongoing drill campaign at La Preciosa, which Avino acquired to complement its producing Avino Mine in Durango.

headline: ANFIELD ENERGY RECEIVES DRAFT STATE APPROVALS FOR UTAH'S SHOOTARING CANYON URANIUM MILL
snippet: Anfield Energy received draft copies of the proposed renewed radioactive materials license and groundwater discharge permit for its Shootaring Canyon Mill from Utah state regulators — a key milestone toward restarting one of only a handful of permitted uranium mills in the United States. Full license approval is targeted for Q2 2027, with a planned production restart to follow. The mill, capable of processing 1,000 tonnes of ore per day when refurbished, would process ore from Anfield's Utah uranium mines.

headline: FOREMOST CLEAN ENERGY DRILLS 1.3% U3O8 OVER 1m AT TUNING FORK ZONE, NORTHERN SASKATCHEWAN
snippet: Foremost Clean Energy reported hole TF-26-30 returning 1.3% uranium oxide over 1.0 metre from its Tuning Fork zone in northern Saskatchewan, continuing a run of high-grade uranium intercepts from the company's 2026 drill program. The result (Oct. 27) confirms continued high-grade mineralization at the Tuning Fork property in Canada's premier uranium district.

headline: CRITICAL METALS COMPLETES EUROPEAN LITHIUM BUYOUT; NASDAQ LISTING AS NEW CRITICAL METALS CORP ON NOV. 6
snippet: Critical Metals Corp's acquisition of European Lithium became legally effective October 27 following Western Australia Supreme Court approval, with European Lithium shares suspended from ASX the same day. The combined entity — focused on a hard-rock lithium project in Austria and critical minerals assets in Greenland and beyond — begins trading as New Critical Metals Corp on Nasdaq on November 6.

headline: SILVER HITS THE MINING DOLDRUMS AT $53 — 45-Year Breakout Being Backtested; Sideline Capital Is the Next Catalyst
snippet: Silver has retreated to the low $50s after setting record highs earlier in 2026, and Metals & Miners argues the metal is backtesting its 45-year cup-and-handle breakout — historically a constructive pattern, but one that requires sideline capital to confirm. The analysis contends that the current demand stack, driven by industrial electrification and solar, is structurally larger than the 2012 silver cycle and that the next significant leg will be powered by retail and institutional money currently on the sidelines.

headline: TECK Q3 TOMORROW WITH HIGHLAND VALLEY STRIKE IN FOCUS — C$1.15 EPS SEEN; 5-DAY WORK STOPPAGE CLOUDS COPPER OUTPUT
snippet: Teck Resources reports Q3 2026 results before market open on October 29, with analyst consensus at approximately C$1.15 EPS and $2.92 billion in revenue. The unresolved Highland Valley Copper strike — now in its fifth day with 1,200 USW workers idled at Canada's largest open-pit copper mine — adds material uncertainty to production guidance for the remainder of 2026. Teck has beaten EPS estimates in each of its last four quarters.

headline: MINING STOCKS LEAD MARKET LOWER AS SUPPORT BREAKS — Gold ETFs Off 9-10%, Silver Underperforms Heading Into Fed
snippet: The weekly technical recap from Silver Gold Alpha documents gold losing roughly 4% and silver falling over 5% in the period leading into the Fed's October 28 decision, while major mining stock ETFs shed 9–10% — significantly underperforming the physical metals. Key chart support levels have broken, and the piece identifies what needs to hold in the GDX and GDXJ to prevent a deeper correction that would drag junior mining equities further below their 2026 highs.
